categories.main_business_segments: Apellis Pharmaceuticals operates primarily in two business segments: Ophthalmology, focused on treatments for geographic atrophy (GA) secondary to age-related macular degeneration (AMD), and Rare Diseases, targeting conditions such as paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria (PNH), C3 glomerulopathy (C3G), and primary immune complex membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis (IC-MPGN). The company’s marketed products are SYFOVRE for GA and EMPAVELI for PNH, with ongoing development for additional indications in nephrology and hematology.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Apellis’s core technology is based on the inhibition of the complement system, specifically targeting the central protein C3 with its lead compound, pegcetacoplan. Pegcetacoplan is a compstatin analogue administered either intravitreally (for ophthalmology) or subcutaneously (for systemic indications). Manufacturing is outsourced to third-party contract manufacturers and involves chemical synthesis, purification, and formulation into vials or prefilled syringes, adhering to cGMP standards.
categories.primary_customers_markets: The company’s primary customers are healthcare professionals and treatment centers specializing in ophthalmology (notably retina specialists and ophthalmologists for SYFOVRE) and rare disease specialists (hematologists and nephrologists for EMPAVELI). End markets include patients with GA, PNH, C3G, IC-MPGN, and potentially other complement-mediated disorders, with a focus on high unmet medical needs.
categories.geographic_coverage: Apellis commercializes its products primarily in the United States, with SYFOVRE approved in the US and Australia, and EMPAVELI approved in the US and several other countries through its partner Sobi (ex-US rights). The company is exploring further international expansion, but currently has limited direct presence outside the US, relying on partners for ex-US commercialization.
categories.supply_chain_position: Apellis operates downstream in the supply chain, focusing on late-stage development, commercialization, and marketing of finished pharmaceutical products. Manufacturing and distribution are outsourced to third-party contract manufacturers and specialty distributors, while the company manages sales, marketing, and patient support programs.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategically, Apellis aims to become a leader in complement-mediated disease therapeutics, prioritizing the expansion of SYFOVRE in GA and EMPAVELI in rare diseases, while advancing its pipeline in nephrology, hematology, and gene editing (via a collaboration with Beam Therapeutics). R&D is focused on new indications for pegcetacoplan, next-generation complement inhibitors (e.g., siRNA APL-3007), and innovative gene-editing approaches targeting the complement system.
categories.revenue_model: The company generates revenue primarily through product sales of SYFOVRE and EMPAVELI in the US, royalties from ex-US sales by Sobi, and milestone payments from collaborations. Revenue is derived from direct sales to specialty distributors, specialty pharmacies, and treatment centers, with additional income from licensing and collaboration agreements.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Apellis faces competition from major pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies developing complement inhibitors and other therapies for GA and rare diseases. Key competitors include Astellas (avacincaptad pegol for GA), AstraZeneca (eculizumab and ravulizumab for PNH), Novartis (iptacopan for PNH and C3G), and Roche/Chugai (crovalimab for PNH). Apellis positions itself as an innovator with first-in-class and best-in-class therapies targeting C3, offering broader complement inhibition than C5 inhibitors.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the year ended December 31, 2024, Apellis reported $611.9 million in US net product revenue from SYFOVRE and $98.1 million from EMPAVELI, with additional royalties from Sobi. The company has experienced rapid revenue growth following product launches but remains unprofitable, with a net loss of $197.9 million in 2024 and an accumulated deficit of $3.0 billion. Apellis employs over 700 people and continues to invest heavily in R&D and commercialization.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Apellis differentiates itself by targeting C3, the central protein in the complement cascade, enabling broad inhibition across all complement pathways. SYFOVRE is positioned as the first and market-leading treatment for GA, offering flexible dosing and increasing efficacy over time, while EMPAVELI is marketed as a best-in-class therapy for PNH and other rare diseases with superior efficacy and self-administration. The company emphasizes its commitment to high unmet needs, robust clinical data, and comprehensive patient support programs.
